title: Introduce sampled prefetch simulation runner and cost thermostat
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: We need a lightweight way to validate prefetch and KV warmup strategies against real traffic shapes without provisioning large-scale dedicated runs. This change adds a sampled prefetch simulation runner (prefetch-sim) that replays a bounded sample of real invocations through a lightweight simulator to measure warmup effectiveness, token-level latency delta, and downstream cost impact. In addition, we introduce a "cost thermostat" component that consumes the sim output to propose safe gating thresholds for aggressive prefetching and quantization profiles, and emits threshold-change proposals as telemetry rather than performing any automatic action.

What this PR does: 1) Adds prefetched-sample collection hooks (server-side sampling at the request router) which annotate invocations with warmup candidates and minimal KV access traces. 2) Implements a simulation runner service (telemetry/prefetch_sim) that consumes historic samples, replays the token access pattern against cached/stubbed KV state, and produces metrics: prefetch_hit_rate, prefetch_latency_delta_ms, simulated_token_cost_delta_usd. 3) Introduces the cost-thermostat service that aggregates sim runs across tenants, computes a cost/latency frontier, and publishes recommended prefetch intensity per tenant as telemetry (no auto-enforcement). 4) Dashboard + alerting: a new Grafana panel (observability/dashboards/prefetch_thermostat.json) surfaces per-tenant frontier curves, 95/99 latency deltas, and expected cost delta; an alert rule suggests review when recommended intensity changes by >20% week-over-week.

Why this is different: Existing tooling measures token cost and rollups after-the-fact. The sim-runner produces an actionable, forward-looking signal that lets us explore tradeoffs offline and tune alerts and rollout policies with better fidelity. The cost thermostat is intentionally advisory to keep operational control with SRE/product teams.

Testing & results: Unit tests for sampler and runner (mocks for KV behavior) were added; integration smoke runs against a 2k-sample corpus show median prefetch_hit_rate 68% and median latency reduction 12ms at an estimated 3.8% token cost increase for one high-throughput tenant. On a separate tenant with cold-prefix-heavy traffic, thermostat recommended intensity 0.35 (from 0.7), avoiding a projected 14% cost increase with only 3ms latency gain.

Rollout plan: feature is behind feature-flag (telemetry.prefetch_sim.enabled). Initial rollout to Canary orgs for 2 weeks, then to low-volume production tenants for an additional 3 weeks. Alerts are advisory initially (no PagerDuty) until SRE signs off.

Related: ENG-1429 (prefetch instrumentation), ENG-1590 (alert tuning experiment).
